newsitem.title: UK: UK govt concerned at London Electricity complaints.
newsitem.headline: UK govt concerned at London Electricity complaints.

text.p: The government on Thursday said it was investigating a rise in complaints against British power supplier London Electricity and will decide whether it should keep its Charter Mark good service award.

Public Service Minister Peter Kilfoyle said on Thursday: "London Electricity won its Charter Mark in 1995 for providing an excellent service but I am concerned by the dramatic rise in the number of complaints received about them in the last six months."
London Electricity was bought up by Entergy UK, a subsidiary of U.S. energy Entergy Corp, earlier this year.

Kilfoyle said officials from the unit which vets service levels for Charter Mark commendations are checking into London Electricity's dealings with customers and will later report back to the judging panel which gives the awards.
The panel will then decide whether the company can keep the award, which are usually given for three years.
